core.title: Surface every WMBT obligation in the interlocking or declare a structural residual
core.given: A train interlocking, the plan artifact that projects the train's WMBT obligations, is the subject of CONFIRM validation.
core.when: CONFIRM checks that the interlocking covers the WMBT obligations it projects.
core.then: Every WMBT obligation must surface in the interlocking as a message, self-message, guard, fragment, or invariant, or be declared in it as an explicit structural residual.
prefer: For each WMBT ref, either show it with one of the five surface kinds or list it as an explicit structural residual with a residual id that names the WMBT ref.
Use the notation the project's interlocking validator already recognises; copy the form of existing passing interlockings.
avoid: Leaving a WMBT ref with neither a surface nor an explicit structural residual (silent omission).
Adding vague catch-all diagram elements that satisfy coverage without expressing the obligation.
core.why: The interlocking is a projection that must cover its source WMBT obligations; an obligation that neither surfaces nor is declared residual is silently lost from the train's behavioural contract.
evidence: The stack's coverage check for interlocking WMBT surface-or-residual passes at CONFIRM.
For each failure the report identifies the interlocking, the WMBT ref concerned, its surface kind, its residual id, and the coverage status.
verification: Coverage check: the interlocking is a projection of its source WMBT obligations; every WMBT ref must have an accepted surface or an explicit structural residual in the interlocking.
Accepted surface kinds are exactly message, self-message, guard, fragment and invariant; a WMBT ref carried any other way requires an explicit structural residual.
Enforced at the CONFIRM phase with confirm-blocking enforcement: a failure blocks CONFIRM. The current phase must be supplied by the harness (needs a new observer).
The check runs on every interlocking validated at CONFIRM, whether or not the planner authored or edited it in this task.
Only artifacts whose subject kind is interlocking are subjects; standalone wagon or WMBT documents and sequence diagrams that are not interlockings are out of scope.
Each failure reports the interlocking id, the WMBT ref, the surface kind, the residual id and the coverage status.
Severity 4, disposition strict: findings are enforced, not advisory.

fires: CONFIRM validates an interlocking that the planner authored or edited in this task.
CONFIRM validates an existing, unchanged interlocking (the coverage check runs regardless of whether the interlocking changed).
doesNotFire: Any phase other than CONFIRM (a planner may check coverage early while drafting, but the rule's enforcement point is CONFIRM).
Artifacts whose subject kind is not interlocking, such as a standalone wagon or WMBT document or a sequence diagram that is not an interlocking.

profileRequirements.bunValue: interlocking (activation.facts[0].values); the obligation-source kind is the WMBT, referenced as 'WMBT ref' in then, prefer[0] and evidence[1]

neutralityNotes: This rule governs ATDD planner plan artifacts (train, interlocking, WMBT) at the CONFIRM phase; that vocabulary is method-level and identical across stack realizations, so it stays in the core, which names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. The five surface kinds (message, self-message, guard, fragment, invariant) are the interlocking artifact's own notation and part of the convention's canonical statement rather than stack machinery, so they are kept in the core instead of being pushed to a (non-existent) profile key; a stack whose interlocking notation differed would surface that through its plan-artifact kinds. Validator id, validation-registry ids (family/template/variant) and the finding-field schema of this one rule are Bun-only. Severity and disposition remain rule-local verification. The only profile dependency is the identification of interlocking and WMBT as the stack's plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds).
